title: Your client pays late
notification: A key client just moved this month's invoice to next month. Part of your revenue won't arrive on time.

lesson.happened: A key client moved their invoice to next month. {amount} of this month's revenue didn't arrive, but your costs still had to be paid on time.

whatIs.title: What are payment terms?
whatIs.text: Payment terms are the deadline on your invoice: 7, 14 or 30 days. Money a client owes you is a receivable. It's yours on paper, but you can't pay rent or salaries with it until it arrives.

lesson.math: This month {revenue} came in instead of the full amount. Your company ended the month with {companyLeft}. The missing {amount} arrives next month. A business cushion worth one month of costs ({costs}) would cover even a big late payment without stress.

quiz.statement: An issued invoice is as good as cash in your account.
quiz.explain: An invoice is a promise. Cash is what you can spend. Plan your month with the cash, not with the invoices.

quiz.statement: A clear payment deadline and a reminder the day after it help you get paid faster.
quiz.explain: Clients pay the invoices that ask clearly first. A 14-day term and a polite reminder beat a 60-day silence.

plan.title: Set clear payment terms
plan.detail: Put a 14-day payment deadline on every invoice and set a calendar reminder to follow up the day after it passes.

title: Your key equipment broke down
notification: The machine your company relies on stopped mid-order. The repair can't wait.

lesson.happened: The machine your company runs on stopped mid-order. The repair bill: {amount}. It wasn't in the budget, and it couldn't wait.

whatIs.title: What is a business cushion?
whatIs.text: A business cushion is cash the company keeps aside only for surprises: a broken machine, a late client, a slow month. A common rule: one to three months of costs. It isn't profit, so you don't pay it out to yourself.

lesson.math: You paid the {amount} repair with money you already had. No loan, no interest: the repair cost exactly {amount}. Borrowed, the same repair would have cost more, because every loan adds interest.
lesson.mathBorrowed: You borrowed {borrowed}. You'll pay back {loanTotal}: {installment} a month for {months} months. That's {interest} extra just in interest. With {amount} set aside in a business cushion, the same repair would have cost exactly {amount}.
lesson.mathPrepared: Your equipment policy paid the {amount} repair. Without it, the company would have paid {amount} from its cash, or borrowed it and paid interest on top.

quiz.statement: A business cushion is money you don't have yet.
quiz.explain: It's money you already earned and chose to keep aside. That's why it's there the day something breaks.

quiz.statement: Borrowing for a repair makes the repair cost more than its bill.
quiz.explain: Interest is the price of not having the money ready. A cushion costs you nothing extra.

plan.title: Start a business cushion
plan.detail: Open a separate savings account for the company and set an automatic monthly transfer (for example 5% of revenue) until it holds one month of costs.

title: Your washing machine died
notification: It stopped mid-cycle. A repair or a new one: either way, you pay this month.

title: Toothache that can't wait
notification: Sharp pain at night. The dentist says root canal, this week.

title: Your phone is broken
notification: It slipped, the screen is dead, and it's the phone you run your business on.

title: You damaged your car
notification: A parking manoeuvre went wrong. The bumper and a headlight need a workshop.

title: A pipe burst at home
notification: Water on the floor, a soaked wall and a plumber who can come today, for a price.

title: You need a doctor now
notification: A sudden illness: private consultation and tests, results needed fast.
